name: Baby bathtub
reason: It makes the first wobbly baths less awkward. A sink works too.
desc: A small plastic tub, often with a sloped insert that holds a newborn.

name: Baby carrier or wrap
reason: Being hands-free is a real relief, but fit is personal, so try one on before buying.
desc: Fabric that holds your baby against your chest. Wraps are a long piece of cloth you tie; structured carriers buckle.

name: Baby gates
reason: Only if you have stairs, and not until your baby starts moving, so it can wait.
desc: Gates that block stairs or doorways, either pressure-mounted or screwed into the wall.

name: Baby monitor
reason: Useful once your baby sleeps out of earshot. If they're in your room, you're the monitor.
desc: A camera or microphone in the nursery that sends sound or video to a parent unit or your phone.

name: Baby shoes
reason: Babies who can't walk don't need shoes. Socks keep feet warm.
desc: Small soft or hard-soled shoes sized for infants.

name: Bassinet
reason: A crib or play yard in your room does the same job.
desc: A small bed on legs that fits next to yours for the first few months.

name: Bodysuits
reason: The everyday base layer. Six to eight in each early size is plenty.
desc: A one-piece top that snaps between the legs, so it stays tucked.

name: Bottle sterilizer
reason: Boiling water or a dishwasher's hot cycle does the same job.
desc: A countertop or microwave device that steams bottles and pump parts clean.

name: Bottle warmer
reason: A bowl of warm water does the same thing, and many babies take milk at room temperature.
desc: A small electric device that heats a bottle of milk.

name: Bottles
reason: You'll need them for formula or pumped milk, and even nursing parents use a few so someone else can feed.
desc: Plastic or glass bottles with a soft nipple. Newborns use the slowest-flow nipple.

name: Bouncer or rocker
reason: A safe spot to set your baby down awake for a few minutes. Not for sleep.
desc: A low, reclined seat on a springy frame that bounces or rocks as your baby moves.

name: Breast pump
reason: Most US health plans cover one, so check before buying.
desc: A hand or electric pump that draws breast milk into a bottle.

name: Burp cloths
reason: You'll go through several a day. Any soft cloth works.
desc: Absorbent cloths you put over your shoulder when burping your baby.

name: Car seat mirror
reason: Add-ons aren't crash-tested with your seat, and you shouldn't be watching the back seat while driving.
desc: A mirror that straps to the back-seat headrest so you can see a rear-facing baby from the driver's seat.

name: Car seat stroller frame
reason: Handy for the first months, but it's outgrown when the infant car seat is.
desc: A lightweight wheeled frame with no seat of its own. Your infant car seat clicks straight into it.

name: Car seat
reason: Every US state requires one, and many hospitals check before you drive home.
desc: A padded seat with a harness that faces the back of the car. Infant versions have a carry handle and click into a base that stays in the car.

name: Changing pad
reason: A towel on the floor works in a pinch.
desc: A contoured, wipeable pad you put on a dresser or the floor for diaper changes.

name: Changing table
reason: A changing pad on a dresser does the same job, and you keep the dresser.
desc: A waist-high table with a rail and shelves, used only for diaper changes.

name: Crib bumpers
reason: Padded bumpers have been banned for sale in the US since 2022. A bare crib is the safe setup.
desc: Padded strips tied around the inside of a crib's slats.
safety: Don't use bumpers, even ones you already have. Take them out of the crib.

name: Crib mattress
reason: Firm, flat, and snug to the crib frame. That's where safe-sleep guidance starts.
desc: A thin, firm mattress sized to fit a standard crib with no gap at the edges.

name: Crib
reason: It's where your baby will sleep for the next two to three years.
desc: A small bed with slatted sides. Most have a mattress height you lower as your baby learns to stand.

name: Diaper bag
reason: Any backpack you already own does the same job.
desc: A bag with lots of pockets for diapers, wipes, and a change of clothes.

name: Diaper pail
reason: It contains the smell better. A lidded trash can you empty daily works fine.
desc: A lidded bin that seals used diapers away.

name: Diapers
reason: Expect eight to twelve a day early on. Don't stockpile the newborn size, because babies outgrow it fast.
desc: Disposable or cloth diapers, sized by your baby's weight.

name: Digital thermometer
reason: It's the first thing your pediatrician will ask about when your baby seems unwell.
desc: A small electronic thermometer that reads temperature in seconds.

name: Fitted crib sheets
reason: Two or three are enough. You'll change them more often than you expect.
desc: Sheets with elastic all the way around, sized for a crib mattress.

name: Formula prep machine
reason: An expensive shortcut for a two-minute task. A kettle and a scoop work.
desc: A countertop machine that mixes formula powder and warm water at the push of a button.

name: Furniture anchors
reason: Cheap straps that keep dressers and shelves from tipping. Install them once and forget them.
desc: Straps or brackets that fix tall furniture to the wall.

name: Glider or nursing chair
reason: You'll spend hours sitting through feeds, and any comfortable chair with arms works.
desc: A padded chair that rocks or glides smoothly, often with a matching footstool.

name: High chair
reason: You won't need it until solids, around six months, so it can wait.
desc: A tall chair with a tray and a harness for meals.

name: Inclined sleeper
reason: Banned for sale in the US since 2022. Babies should sleep flat.
desc: A sleeper that holds a baby at an angle instead of flat.
safety: Don't use one for sleep, even one you already have. Inclined sleepers have been linked to infant deaths and were recalled.

name: Nail clippers or file
reason: Newborn nails are sharp and grow fast.
desc: Small clippers or an emery file sized for tiny nails.

name: Nursing pillow
reason: It takes strain off your arms and back during feeds. A regular pillow works for many parents.
desc: A firm, C-shaped pillow that wraps around your waist to raise your baby during feeds.

name: Pacifiers
reason: Many babies like them, and they're cheap enough to try. Some won't take one at all.
desc: A soft nipple on a shield, for sucking between feeds.

name: Play yard (travel crib)
reason: Useful for travel or a second floor, not needed if you have a crib.
desc: A foldable crib with mesh sides that packs into a bag.

name: Sleep positioner or wedge
reason: The FDA and AAP advise against them. Flat and bare is the safe setup.
desc: Foam wedges or bolsters meant to hold a sleeping baby in one position.
safety: Don't use one, even one you already have. Lay your baby on their back on a firm, flat mattress with nothing else in the crib.

name: Sleep sack
reason: Loose blankets aren't safe in the crib, and this is how you keep your baby warm instead.
desc: A wearable blanket with arm holes that zips over pajamas.

name: Smart sock or vitals monitor
reason: The AAP doesn't recommend them for preventing SIDS, and false alarms add worry rather than remove it.
desc: A sock or clip that tracks your baby's heart rate and oxygen and alerts your phone.

name: Stroller
reason: You'll use it most days for the first few years.
desc: A wheeled seat you push. Many fold down for the trunk, and some recline flat for newborns.

name: Swaddle
reason: Many newborns settle better wrapped. You'll stop once your baby starts trying to roll.
desc: A blanket or zip-up wrap that holds a newborn's arms snugly at their sides.

name: White noise machine
reason: It helps some babies sleep through household noise. A free phone app is a fine test first.
desc: A small speaker that plays steady background sound.

name: Wipe warmer
reason: Nice idea, but most parents stop using it within a few weeks. It's not a safety or comfort issue either way.
desc: A plug-in box that keeps a pack of wipes warm.

name: Wipes
reason: You'll use them for far more than diapers.
desc: Soft, damp cloths in a resealable pack.

name: Zip-up sleepers
reason: You'll appreciate a zipper at 3 a.m. Snaps are slower.
desc: Footed one-piece pajamas that zip from neck to ankle.
